panels.description: Multi-bit memory errors. Any non-zero value indicates failing silicon that can cause kernel panics or silent data corruption.
panels.title: Uncorrectable ECC Errors

panels.description: Single-bit memory errors corrected by ECC. A rising rate is an early warning of a degrading DIMM.
panels.title: Correctable ECC Errors

panels.description: Number of drives reporting less than 20% of their rated endurance remaining. Schedule proactive replacement.
panels.title: Drives Below 20% Life

panels.description: Drives with sectors waiting for remap. These are latent media failures and often precede data loss.
panels.title: Drives With Pending Sectors

panels.description: Total remapped (bad) blocks across all drives. Growth indicates media degradation.
panels.title: Reallocated Blocks

panels.description: Combined address parity and CRC errors across interconnects and PCIe buses.

targets.expr: (sum(idrac_telemetry_address_parity_error_total{instance=~"$instance", job=~"$job"}) or vector(0)) + (sum(idrac_telemetry_crc_error_count{instance=~"$instance", job=~"$job"}) or vector(0))

panels.title: Bus Errors (Parity + CRC)

panels.description: Storage or hardware controller command timeouts. Persistent timeouts point to a failing controller, cable or backplane.
panels.title: Command Timeouts

panels.description: Flash erase failures reported by SSDs/NVMe drives. Any non-zero value means the media can no longer reliably erase blocks.
panels.title: Erase Failures

panels.description: Rate of ECC errors per second. A sustained non-zero correctable rate or any uncorrectable rate requires DIMM replacement.
panels.title: ECC Error Rate

panels.description: Cumulative ECC error counters. A step increase marks the moment a DIMM started failing.
panels.title: ECC Error Totals

panels.description: Per-DIMM ECC error counters. Use this table to identify the specific module that needs replacement.
panels.title: ECC Errors by Module

panels.description: Remaining rated endurance per drive. Below 20% schedule replacement; below 10% replace immediately.
panels.title: Drive Life Remaining

panels.description: Endurance consumption trend. A steep downward slope indicates write amplification or an overloaded drive.
panels.title: Drive Life Remaining Over Time

panels.description: Bad sector indicators. Reallocated blocks are already-remapped media; pending sectors are waiting for remap and are the more urgent signal.
panels.title: Bad Sector Indicators

panels.description: Drive-level failure counters: uncorrectable errors, total media writes and erase failures.
panels.title: Drive Failure Counters

panels.description: Consolidated SMART view per drive for triage and replacement planning.
panels.title: Drive SMART Detail

panels.description: Address parity errors and CRC errors indicate interconnect or PCIe bus integrity problems (riser, cable, slot or endpoint).
panels.title: Bus Integrity Errors

panels.description: Controller and storage command timeouts over time. Repeated timeouts usually precede drive dropouts.
panels.title: Command Timeouts Over Time

panels.description: Aggregated bus and controller fault indicator. ALARM means at least one parity, CRC or timeout fault was reported.

targets.expr: (sum(idrac_telemetry_address_parity_error_total{instance=~"$instance", job=~"$job"}) or vector(0)) + (sum(idrac_telemetry_crc_error_count{instance=~"$instance", job=~"$job"}) or vector(0)) + (sum(idrac_telemetry_command_timeout{instance=~"$instance", job=~"$job"}) or vector(0))

panels.title: Bus & Controller Fault Alarm
